findings.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3`: `cook_method` defaults to `1` (`raw_html`), causing existing and ordinary new posts to bypass cooking and sanitization and render user-supplied raw content directly
`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`: Feed-provided HTML is imported using `raw_html` without sanitization, allowing malicious scripts or event handlers to execute under the forum's origin
`lib/topic_retriever.rb:16-53`: Only the initial URL hostname is validated; redirects can reach loopback, link-local, or private-network addresses, enabling SSRF
`app/models/topic_embed.rb:14`: `url` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted HTML attribute, allowing a same-host URL containing an apostrophe to inject attributes or markup into raw HTML
`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17`: Message origins are validated with substring matching and `e.source` is not checked, allowing a distinct prefix-matching origin to send iframe resize messages
`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15`: Unknown-URL requests enqueue jobs before worker-side throttling, allowing clients with spoofed Referer headers to flood the Sidekiq queue with no-op jobs
`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`: `i.content.scrub` assumes every feed item has content; description-only RSS items cause `NoMethodError` and abort the polling run
`lib/topic_retriever.rb:39-52`: Embed URLs are keyed by unnormalized strings, so query, fragment, hostname-case, or default-port variants can create duplicate topics

`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-44`: The spec expects direct `TopicRetriever` invocation even though the controller now uses `Jobs.enqueue`, causing test failure and leaving asynchronous behavior untested

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3`: `cook_method` defaults to `1` (`raw_html`), causing existing and ordinary new posts to bypass cooking and sanitization and render user-supplied raw content directly

adjudication.rationale: The migration sets default value of 1 for cook_method. Looking at Post.cook_methods in app/models/post.rb, the enum is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` which means :regular = 1 and :raw_html = 2 (Enum typically starts at 1). So default of 1 means :regular, not :raw_html. The finding incorrectly states that 1 maps to raw_html. However, examining the cook method in post.rb shows it checks `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` to skip cooking. Since default is 1 (:regular), existing posts would still be cooked normally. The finding appears to misunderstand the enum mapping - the default of 1 corresponds to :regular (first enum value), not :raw_html.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`: Feed-provided HTML is imported using `raw_html` without sanitization, allowing malicious scripts or event handlers to execute under the forum's origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in poll_feed.rb line 35: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` followed by `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. In topic_embed.rb, the import method uses `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` which bypasses cooking/sanitization (as shown in post.rb lines 131-133: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). The ruby-readability library in import_remote only allows specific tags but the poll_feed path directly imports RSS content without such filtering. This means malicious RSS feed content with scripts or event handlers would be rendered as raw HTML without sanitization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb:16-53`: Only the initial URL hostname is validated; redirects can reach loopback, link-local, or private-network addresses, enabling SSRF

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real SSRF vulnerability. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, the invalid_host? method only checks if the hostname matches SiteSetting.embeddable_host at lines 14-18. However, the actual HTTP fetch happens in fetch_http (line 50-53) which calls TopicEmbed.import_remote. Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 44-49, import_remote uses open(url).read without any redirect validation. An attacker could provide a URL that passes the initial hostname check but redirects to internal/private network addresses (127.0.0.1, 169.254.x.x, 10.x.x.x, etc.), enabling Server-Side Request Forgery. The diff shows no protection against redirect-based SSRF attacks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15`: Unknown-URL requests enqueue jobs before worker-side throttling, allowing clients with spoofed Referer headers to flood the Sidekiq queue with no-op jobs

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at embed_controller.rb lines 8-16, when topic_id is nil (no existing embed), the code immediately enqueues a job via `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` before any throttling occurs. The throttling logic is in TopicRetriever (lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 22-31) which only runs AFTER the job is dequeued by Sidekiq workers. The ensure_embeddable method only checks that embeddable_host is set and referer matches, but Referer headers can be spoofed. This means attackers can flood the Sidekiq queue with jobs by sending requests with different embed_urls and spoofed Referer headers matching the embeddable_host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb:39-52`: Embed URLs are keyed by unnormalized strings, so query, fragment, hostname-case, or default-port variants can create duplicate topics

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the code. Looking at the diff, TopicEmbed uses `embed_url` as a key (line 17 in topic_embed.rb: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and the database has a unique index on embed_url. The URLs are stored as-is without normalization. In topic_retriever.rb lines 39-52, the `perform_retrieve` method checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` using the raw URL. If the same logical URL is accessed with different representations (e.g., 'http://example.com' vs 'http://example.com/' vs 'http://EXAMPLE.com'), they would be treated as different URLs, potentially creating duplicate topics. This is a correctness bug in the URL deduplication logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-44`: The spec expects direct `TopicRetriever` invocation even though the controller now uses `Jobs.enqueue`, causing test failure and leaving asynchronous behavior untested

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the embed_controller.rb shows that when no topic_id is found, it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` (line 14). However, the test in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb lines 40-44 expects `TopicRetriever.new` to be called directly and `retriever.retrieve` to be invoked. This is a mismatch - the controller enqueues a job, but the test expects synchronous TopicRetriever invocation. The test will fail because TopicRetriever.new is never called directly by the controller; instead Jobs.enqueue is called. This is a real bug in the test code.
